title: 2400-baud modems
headline: TRADE PRESS: 2400 baud modems promised 'by next year'. Nobody believes it.

title: Monopoly breakup
headline: TV: the national phone monopoly is broken into pieces. The pieces look annoyed.

title: Hobbyist mail networks
headline: Bulletin boards start passing mail to each other overnight. Long-distance bills explode.

title: Multi-line hunt groups for small business
headline: The phone company will now roll a busy line to the next free one. For a fee.

title: Small-business billing software
headline: A floppy-disk billing package goes on sale. The manual is heavier than the computer.

title: Network management protocol
headline: Engineers agree on a way for equipment to report its own health. Equipment is unaware.

title: 14.4k modems
headline: 14,400 bits per second. Magazines call it 'the end of waiting'.

title: The World Wide Web
headline: A physicist posts something called 'the web' to a newsgroup. Almost nobody notices.

title: Dial-in authentication servers
headline: One server to check every dial-in password. One server to fail them all.

title: Graphical web browsers on sale
headline: You can now buy a browser in a box. Queues outside the computer shop.

title: Consumer ADSL
headline: Always-on internet over the same copper as your phone. 'Always' is doing a lot of work.

title: The touchscreen phone
headline: A phone that is mostly screen. Data usage graphs develop a new shape.

title: 4G / LTE
headline: Mobile data fast enough to make home broadband nervous.

title: 5G
headline: 5G launches. Nobody can explain what it is for, including the people selling it.

title: Exchange 0
headline: WORK ORDER: Exchange 0. Assigned engineer: you.
